main.claim: Upload any image and get a ready-to-paste text prompt that describes its subject, style, lighting, colors and camera. Free, with no account needed. The prompt is ready in a few seconds.

sections.heading: How to turn a picture into a prompt
sections.body:
Open [Image to Prompt](https://image-to-prompt.lazur.app/) in the browser you already use. You do not need an app or an account.

1. Upload your image, or drop it onto the page. Files can be up to 15 MB.
2. Choose the image AI you plan to use: Midjourney, DALL·E, Stable Diffusion, or any image AI.
3. Wait a few seconds for the prompt to appear.
4. Copy the prompt with one click and paste it into your image AI.

**Read the prompt before you paste it.** It describes what the picture shows, so change any word that does not match the picture you want in your head.

sections.heading: What the prompt covers
sections.body:
The prompt is one paragraph. It starts with the subject, then adds the style, the lighting, the colors, the composition, and the camera or medium. A photo gets camera words such as lens and light direction. A painting or drawing gets the medium and the brushwork.

If the image AI you chose can use one, the prompt ends with a line that starts with “Negative prompt:”. That line lists what to leave out, such as blur or extra limbs. Delete the line if your image AI does not use it.

You can read the prompt as a short photo caption that is also a set of instructions. That is why it works in most image tools without any changes.

sections.heading: Get a better prompt from your image
sections.body:
The tool describes what it can see, so a sharp photo with one clear subject gives a clearer prompt than a dark, blurry or crowded one. Crop out anything you do not want in the description before you upload.

Each run counts toward your daily limit. If the first prompt misses something, change one or two words in it instead of starting again from a new image. Small word changes often change the picture a lot, and you keep the parts that already work.

sections.heading: Free use and your photo
sections.body:
You get 3 runs a day for free. Leave an email and you get 3 more. No account is needed for either.

The tool runs Google Gemini on Lazur's servers, so your image is sent there to write the prompt. Do not upload a picture of a person, a document or anything else you are not allowed to share.

sections.heading: Prompts every day
sections.body: If you write image prompts every day, Lazur is a Mac app for that: hold two keys and talk, and it types into whatever app you are in. Windows is coming.

pages.description: Turn any photo into a prompt you can paste into Gemini. Upload your image, copy the text, then create the picture in Gemini. Free, no account.
pages.claim: Upload your photo here and copy the prompt it writes, then paste it into Gemini's image tool at gemini.google.com. The prompt covers subject, style, light and camera. Free, with no account needed.

sections.heading: Make the prompt, then the picture
sections.body:
Start here, then move to Gemini. First, turn your photo into a prompt:

1. Open [Image to Prompt](https://image-to-prompt.lazur.app/) and upload the photo. Files up to 15 MB work.
2. Choose the option for any image AI. This tool is not built only for Gemini, so pick the general option.
3. Copy the prompt with one click.

The prompt is one paragraph with the subject, style, lighting, colors and camera or medium. Gemini reads plain sentences, so you can paste it as it is.

sections.heading: Create the image in Gemini
sections.body:
These are the steps from Google's Gemini help page for creating an image. The page says the image is made with Nano Banana.

1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
2. At the top left, click the sidebar icon labeled “Open Sidebar”, then click “Images”.
3. Type or paste your prompt, or choose a template instead.

Google's steps are on its [Gemini help page](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14286560). Check that page if Gemini's menus look different on your screen.

sections.heading: Add your photo as a reference
sections.body:
Google's page says you can also upload reference images when you create an image. Upload the same photo next to your prompt to give Gemini a picture to follow.

The prompt then adds the words for what you want to change, such as the light, the style or the mood. A reference photo shows the model the subject, and the words steer the rest. Try it once with and once without the reference, and compare the two results side by side.

sections.heading: Edit a photo you already have
sections.body:
If you want to change a photo instead of making a new one, Google's help page gives these steps:

1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
2. At the top left, click “Open Sidebar”, then click “Library”.
3. Find your image and click it. To edit a photo from your device, upload it.
4. Under the image, click “Chat”.
5. In the text box at the bottom, type your edit request, then click “Submit”.

Keep the edit request short and direct, such as “make the sky a deep orange at sunset”. A long list of changes is harder for the model to follow in one go.

sections.heading: What this tool does not do
sections.body:
The tool does not make the picture. It writes the text, and Gemini or another image AI makes the image from that text. Results can differ from one run to the next, so generate two or three and keep the one closest to what you want.

Your photo is sent to Lazur's servers, where Google Gemini writes the prompt. Use only images you are allowed to share.

If you write Gemini prompts every day, Lazur is a Mac app that types for you: hold two keys and talk, and it types into whatever app you are in.

faq.q: Is the image prompt tool free to use with Gemini?
faq.a: The prompt tool is free. You get 3 runs a day, and 3 more if you leave an email, with no account needed. Creating the picture happens in Gemini, so Google's own terms for Gemini apply there.

faq.q: Does Gemini need a special prompt format?
faq.a: No special format is needed. Gemini takes plain sentences, so the one-paragraph prompt from this tool works as it is. Change any word that does not match the picture you want, then submit it.

faq.q: Can I upload my photo into Gemini as well?
faq.a: Yes. Google's help page says you can upload reference images when you create an image. A reference photo helps Gemini match what is in your picture, and the prompt adds the style or light you want.

Add the photo after the prompt, then ask ChatGPT to create the picture the way the prompt describes it.
